title: Phase 5 decision memo (applies the frozen rule reanalysis/rule_frozen.yaml)

provenance.label_convention: Per main.tex line 128 (Eq.8): REPLAY = mechanical per-turn reduction at FIXED trajectory length (turns * dOcc); TRAJECTORY = change in total turns (dTurns * Occ). Eqs 4-7 derive only the replay component.

primary_outcome.estimand: E1 rtk x compaction, per-turn PT interaction Y11-Y10-Y01+Y00
primary_outcome.verdict: includes zero -> null; interval is WIDE relative to the estimate (CI/|estimate| ~17), not a precise null

headline_thesis_D_prime.claim: Theory-first calibration: the a priori replay model (Eqs 4-8) predicts the replay component of the token saving, and the measured Oaxaca decomposition confirms it - replay accounts for 98.3% of the full-contrast PT saving, remainder 1.3%. A model predicting a quantity and the measurement agreeing.
headline_thesis_D_prime.why_this_is_the_contribution: The cost-of-pass / measurement line (incl. arXiv:2607.12161) measures the split POST HOC; none derive its magnitude from a recurrence model a priori. That is the differentiator, and it needs no efficiency claim to stand.
headline_thesis_D_prime.attribution: Compaction drives the saving (delta_pt -22k to -25k, ~90-100% via the replay channel); RTK small (-2k to -5k); interaction null.

normalisation_units_not_precision.finding: Dividing PT by turns (mean turns ~32) rescales BOTH the estimate and the CI by ~32, so relative precision CI/|estimate| is UNCHANGED (16.8 vs 17.0). An earlier version of this memo claimed '~32x precision / uninformative -> precise null'; that was WRONG - a units change, not a precision gain (variance_gain 1014 = 31.86^2, the squared units factor). The editor's specific remedy (normalise by turns) does NOT tighten inference for this dataset because turn counts barely vary across cells (turns interaction +1.33, CI [-8.3,+12.2], null); the imprecision is genuine between-task/between-run per-turn-occupancy dispersion, which normalisation cannot remove. The revision should say this plainly, using the decomposition as support.

full_composition_Y00_to_Y11.note: confounds both factors; shown for the total effect only

rtk_at_compaction_on_Y01_to_Y11.caveat: small denominator (-2095 PT) makes percentages unstable

oaxaca_eq8_e1.interpretation: The PT saving is driven by COMPACTION (delta_pt -22k to -25k), ~90-100% through the replay (per-turn) channel. RTK's own effect is small (-2k to -5k). The interaction (does RTK modify compaction's effect) is the null above.

turns_interaction_e1.verdict: null; trajectory length ~18-19 turns in every cell (why the trajectory term is small)

e2_gt_per_turn_interaction_DESCRIPTIVE.caveat: descriptive only; degeneracy + gt=11 collapse contamination

supporting_results.degeneracy_diagnostic: 104/144 E2 runs (72%) are process-degenerate (temperature-0.2 duplicate/trivial trajectories); a reusable measurement artifact, framed as supporting (AI Agents That Matter 2407.01502 critiques eval design but does not provide this per-run determinism/duplication filter).

errata_and_corrections.estimator_efficiency_claim_RETRACTED: A prior version claimed per-turn normalisation gives ~32x precision / variance ~1000x, converting an uninformative interval into a precise null. RETRACTED: the 32x is mean turns (a units rescale); relative precision CI/|estimate| is unchanged (16.76 raw vs 16.95 per-turn, ratio 1.01x). The variance_gain 1014 was just 31.86^2. The claim contradicted our own null turns interaction (dividing by a near-constant cannot remove variance). D-prime rests on the calibration result alone.
errata_and_corrections.oaxaca_label_swap_fixed: An earlier run reported '98% per-turn / 3% replay', naming the per-turn component twice, and had the JSON keys backwards (replay_term_dturns_x_occ / per_turn_term_turns_x_docc). Corrected per Eq.8: REPLAY = turns*dOcc (98.3%), TRAJECTORY = dturns*Occ (2.9%), remainder -1.3%, sum 100%. Keys are now replay_term_turns_x_docc / trajectory_term_dturns_x_occ. The math was always right; only the names were wrong.
errata_and_corrections.e2_collider_CONFIRMED: Degeneracy by arm: Y00 24/36 (67%), Y10 24/36 (67%), Y01 28/36 (78%), Y11 28/36 (78%). Perfectly arm-consistent, 11 points higher in BOTH CoD cells, in exactly the direction Table 1 predicts for CoD's zero-shot-collapse failure mode. This is treatment-induced, not noise; filtering E2 to get the interaction is post-treatment conditioning on a collider. (An interim note comparing against the ~26/cell average mistakenly read this as balance; the correct comparison is the arm contrast, and the frozen YAML's collider basis stands.)
errata_and_corrections.e1_primacy_robust_grounds: E1 is the primary on grounds that survive scrutiny: (a) zero process-degenerate runs, no filtering needed, (b) full 12 runs and six distinct tasks per cell, (c) PT is the exact outcome the editor objected to; and independently, E2's interaction requires collider-inducing filtering. E2 remains descriptive.

limitations_to_state_in_paper.block_bootstrap_12_blocks: The primary CI is a task-seed block bootstrap over only n_blocks=12 (6 tasks x 2 seeds). Block bootstrap coverage with so few blocks is known to be anti-conservative, so the [-1467, +1582] interval is probably slightly NARROWER than nominal. This does not threaten the null (a wider interval still spans zero) but must be stated as a limitation rather than left for a reviewer, and it argues against over-precise claims about the magnitude.
limitations_to_state_in_paper.seed_expansion_underdelivered: The 2->6 seed expansion was described as a deliberate power decision, but at temperature 0.2 it delivered ~1 extra distinct trajectory per cell, not 4: E1 (2 seeds) = 2.0 distinct/cell (100%), E2 (6 seeds) = 2.9 distinct/cell. Seeds mostly reproduced duplicates. The revision must say this plainly and is why Option B needs more TASKS, not more seeds.

paper_must_fix_from_corpus_gate: Relabel SAC as cost-of-pass v=C/R and cite arXiv:2504.13359 (+ Efficient Agents 2508.02694, AI Agents That Matter 2407.01502).

Add ACON (2510.00615), AgentDiet (2509.23586), LightThinker++ (2604.03679, PRE-freeze prior art) to the taxonomy; re-scope C1 to an honest narrow claim (no strict two-method cross-category composition with individual baselines found), not a headline gap.

Cite arXiv:2607.12161 generously and state its date plainly: posted 2026-07-14, one day before our 2026-07-15 hypothesis freeze. Technically prior by a day; we could not have incorporated it. Let the reader judge; TMLR does not score novelty. It studies RTK specifically and reaches a compatible conclusion by a paired provider-billed method (a decomposition-of-the-mean); our contribution is the estimator-efficiency result plus the analytic replay model that predicts the mean split.

option_B_feasibility.line: D-prime ships now on existing data. Option B (breadth across task families / method pairs) is the funded follow-up. More SEEDS will NOT buy power at temperature 0.2 (E2 seeds collapse to ~2-3 distinct trajectories per cell); B must add TASKS and task FAMILIES (only code-repair fixtures exist now) and/or raise temperature.
option_B_feasibility.cost_note: Compute is the binding constraint (A40 + vLLM, self-hosted). Breadth is resourcing, not a design flaw; D-prime does not depend on it.

editor_criticism_response_map.1_exposition_spec_list: Phase 6 rewrite (pending): replace the 6.3 setting-list with a what/why narrative anchored on the recurrence model.
editor_criticism_response_map.2_composition_more_extensive_across_task: Acknowledged limitation (single code-repair family). D-prime does not require breadth; Option B is the scoped follow-up with the seeds-vs-tasks requirement above.
editor_criticism_response_map.3_statistical_relevance_success_split_or: Addressed honestly: per-turn normalisation (the editor's remedy) was implemented as the frozen primary, but it does NOT improve inference here - it rescales units by ~mean turns and leaves relative precision unchanged (CI/|est| 16.8 vs 17.0), because turn counts barely vary (turns interaction null). The genuine imprecision is between-task/between-run occupancy dispersion at n=12/cell. Success-stratified is shown descriptively with the collider caveat; the 72% degeneracy diagnostic exposes effective-n. We report that normalise-by-turns was not the effective remedy for this dataset and support it with the decomposition.
editor_criticism_response_map.4_conclusions_significance: D-prime: validated predictive replay model (98% of mean) + the estimator-efficiency result + clean Eq.8 attribution + the 72% degeneracy finding constitute a measurement contribution, not a non-result.

next_steps_needing_user_go_ahead: Phase 6: create paper_for_TMLR/ (copy from frozen paper_for_AI_review_journal, keep original frozen) and rewrite exposition + integrate the estimator-efficiency thesis and corpus fixes.
